correctness.rationale: All maximal independent sets are A and B when t=0. For t>=1 every independent set meeting both sides lies in a unique missing pair {a_i,b_i}; these pairs are maximal; each entire side remains maximal iff its cardinality is at least 2. For t=1, equating the weights of surviving maximal sets yields the exact displayed positive free parameters, with singleton-side exceptions. For t>=2 both entire sides and P1,P2 are maximal; their weights must all equal W but P1 and P2 are disjoint, so w(P1∪P2)=2W=w(A∪B). Since P1∪P2 is a proper subset of A∪B if a+b>4, positivity is impossible. The remaining a=b=t=2 yields two disjoint edges with all solutions (p,q,q,p). Finite independent maximal-independent-set enumeration checked representative boundary cases, and source verify.py fully inspected; no small finite experiment is used in place of the unbounded proof.

value.rationale: Asks a natural sharp robustness question: when does deleting a matching of size t destroy positive weight equalization of maximal independent sets in complete bipartite graphs? The one-edge boundary, exceptional 2K2 and full positive-integer cone are a self-contained exact structural classification, more useful than a single small graph check despite short obstruction proof.

final_claim: For G=K_{a,b} with a matching of size t deleted, a,b>=1, 0<=t<=min(a,b), positive-integer levelability holds exactly if t<=1 or (a,b,t)=(2,2,2); all surviving positive-integer weight functions are explicitly classified by side-sum and deleted-endpoint equalities.
limitations: Classification does not cover deletion of arbitrary cross edges, other graph families, or all real well-covered weights outside positive cone.
